chapter: Teens with the Salt City Six
title: School band: St. Mary's, Prof Stanley and learning to read
summary: Sent out of two schools, he lands in the Cortland high school band where Burton Stanley tells him his reading will catch up.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: year. That was between my junior and senior year. And I played with the high school band all of that time. I had actually, to back it up a little bit, from Parker School up the street, for disciplinary reasons, I was sent to St. Mary’s School which is right about seven houses that way. They didn’t have a band. So they figured — so here I am not really learning how to read music as well as I’d like to have, and Burton Stanley was a professor up at Potsdam, was the band director there. And he played a job with a big band up in Syracuse with Spiegle, up at Hotel Syracuse. I sat in and he said to my father, “you’ve got to let me have him. You’ve got to send him to the high school.” Well I was asked, delicately asked, to leave St. Mary’s School for disciplinary reasons once again. Not like kids today carrying guns to school, but just a troublemaker you know, or whatever, talking back, that kind of thing. So I get to the high school and I went right to Burton Stanley and the high school band director and I said, “Prof,” we called him Prof Stanley. Corky Fabrizio took his place because he went up to Potsdam. And I said, “Prof, you’d better put me in the junior band.” I said, “my eyes, I’m not going to be able to read this music in senior band.” He said, “let me worry about that.” He said, “your eyes will catch up to your hands, don’t worry.”
No. My reading. Yeah. “Your eyes will catch up to your hands.”
Okay. I didn’t quite understand, if your eyesight was bad.

No I mean it’s like “nice eyes baby” you know, in other words like you can read real well. And it didn’t take too long. I was always hoping for a sunny day during marching band season because then we’d go outside and be practicing marching band stuff, which was no problem. But on rainy days we had to go into symphonic or concert band and oh man, that was, for me, I just didn’t enjoy that.
